result:
Done. PR #156 is finished and out of draft.

**What the resume asked for, and its state:**

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Merge `origin/master` | Clean, 59 commits, no conflicts |
| `selftest.sh` green | **Red — 501/10, but it's master's, not mine** (below) |
| Push + `gh pr ready 156` | Done; `isDraft: false`, `MERGEABLE` |
| `gh-label.sh add 156 harness` | Applied |
| CI | Android SUCCESS, Desktop build SUCCESS on the new head |

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish** (now recorded in `docs/lanes/wbufclip/NOTES.md`): nothing was wrong with the work — the PR was simply never marked ready. The trap worth naming is that this brief's real outcome is *blocked*, and a blocked outcome feels unfinished, so draft felt consistent. It isn't: a blocked brief with its blocker measured is finished under step 6 of the lane contract.

**Two things found while finishing:**

1. **`.gitignore` had eaten the lane's most actionable artifact.** `docs/testing/wbuf31_clipf_phase.patch` — the one-integer upstream source change — was claimed in the PR body and NOTES as delivered and `git apply --check` verified. Both true, and the file was never committed: `.gitignore:20` is `*.patch`, so the `git add` was a silent no-op. `git status` stayed clean, push succeeded, CI went green; it existed only in this worktree and would have been lost at fold. Committed now with `git add -f`. Caught only by diffing the body's `Files:` line against `git diff --name-only`. I also posted a correction on #31, whose earlier comment pointed readers at that dangling path.

2. **`selftest.sh` is red on `origin/master` itself.** 10 failures, deterministic, all in `selftest.d/86-fold-regressed.sh`. `git diff --stat origin/master HEAD -- docs/testing/jobs/` is empty on this head, so the run exercises master's code byte-for-byte; my whole diff is three write-ups, NOTES, and two `wbuf_*` tools. The fragment arrived with PR #145 (`lane/foldregress`) and `fold.sh` was touched afterwards by PR #151 (`lane/localtime`) — that ordering is where I'd look, but both files belong to another lane, so I reported rather than touched. Flagged in a PR comment for the board.

I marked ready on green CI rather than holding for someone else's red — holding would have repeated exactly the defect this resume exists to fix. Every lane running `selftest.sh` as its own gate will hit that red until `lane.foldregress` owns it, so it may be worth dispatching promptly.
